profile.summary: PlantCaduceus (short name PlantCAD) is a DNA language model for flowering plants, pretrained on the genomes of 16 angiosperm species. It reads 512-bp DNA windows one nucleotide at a time, looking at both strands. Its embeddings feed small classifiers that predict translation start and stop sites and splice sites in species it was not trained on, and its masked-base likelihoods give a zero-shot score for how deleterious a single-nucleotide variant is.
profile.summary_source_locator: README: PlantCAD overview; Paper: Abstract, Introduction, Fig. 1 caption

summary_quotes.text: PlantCaduceus, with its short name of **PlantCAD**, is a plant DNA LM based on the [Caduceus](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.03234) architecture
We introduce PlantCaduceus, a plant DNA LM that learns evolutionary conservation patterns in 16 angiosperm genomes by modeling both DNA strands simultaneously.
The input for PlantCaduceus consists of 512-bp DNA sequences with 15% of positions randomly masked.

PlantCAD showed state-of-the-art cross species performance in predicting TIS, TTS, Splice Donor and Splice Acceptor. The zero-shot of PlantCAD enables identifying genome-wide deleterious mutations and known causal variants in Arabidopsis, Sorghum and Maize.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: PlantCaduceus uses the Caduceus architecture, which builds on the Mamba state-space sequence model and adds bi-directionality and reverse complement (RC) equivariance, so both DNA strands are modelled together. It uses single-nucleotide tokens. Pretraining is masked language modelling: 15% of positions in each 512-bp window are masked and the model is trained with cross-entropy loss on them. Following GPN, the pretraining set down-samples noncoding regions and down-weights repeats. Downstream, frozen embeddings train XGBoost or linear classifiers, and the zero-shot score is the log-likelihood difference between the reference and alternate allele at a masked position.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Introduction; Fig. 1 caption; Results; Methods; README: PlantCAD overview

quotes.text: which extends the efficient [Mamba](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.00752) linear-time sequence modeling framework to incorporate bi-directionality and reverse complement equivariance, specifically designed for DNA sequences
The pretraining objective is cross-entropy loss on the masked positions.
we generated an unbiased genomic dataset for pretraining by down-sampling noncoding regions and down-weighting repetitive sequences
Both approaches were applied on frozen embeddings extracted from the last hidden state of PlantCaduceus

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: PlantCAD comes in four sizes, named by their number of Caduceus blocks: PlantCaduceus_l20, l24, l28 and l32, all with a 512-bp input. The model card recommends the largest, l32, for zero-shot scoring. The same repository now also hosts PlantCAD2, a later generation with an 8192-bp input and separate checkpoints (Small, Medium, Large); it is a different model and is not covered here. A result should name the checkpoint and its Hugging Face revision; the listing read on 2026-11-26 gives l32 at e624c13c, l28 at 5ac1d5e7, l24 at 8c41e4d5 and l20 at d1b3c7d4.
sections.source_locator: README: Model summary; model card: Model Overview; Hugging Face listing; Paper: Results, Table 1

quotes.text: we trained a series of PlantCaduceus models with varying depths (20, 24, 28, and 32 Caduceus blocks)
We would highly recommend using the largest model ([PlantCaduceus_l32](https://huggingface.co/kuleshov-group/PlantCaduceus_l32)) for the zero-shot score estimation.

sections.title: Evaluation in the paper
sections.body: The authors trained XGBoost and linear classifiers on Arabidopsis labels for translation initiation and termination sites and splice donor and acceptor sites, then tested them on species in the pretraining set (Oryza sativa, Sorghum bicolor) and outside it (Gossypium hirsutum, Glycine max, Zea mays). They compared PlantCaduceus with other DNA language models including GPN and AgroNT. For variants, they compared zero-shot scores with phyloP, phastCons, GPN and AgroNT. The claim of best cross-species performance is the authors'.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Bi-directional, reverse-complement equivariant DNA language model trained by masked language modelling.
facts.source_locator: Model card: Model Overview; README: PlantCAD overview

quotes.text: PlantCaduceus is a DNA language model pre-trained on 16 Angiosperm genomes.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Caduceus blocks built on the Mamba state-space model. l20: 20 layers, hidden size 384; l24: 24 layers, 512; l28: 28 layers, 768; l32: 32 layers, 1024. The l32 config sets rcps true and vocab_size 8.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: DNA sequence of at most 512 bp, tokenised one nucleotide per token.

quotes.text: The "Max Input Length" is a hard limit

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Masked-base predictions and per-nucleotide hidden states. The hidden state holds a forward and a reverse-complement half, which the README averages into one embedding. Log-likelihood differences give zero-shot variant scores.
facts.source_locator: README: Quick example, Usage guides; Paper: Results

quotes.text: # Average forward and reverse complement embeddings
Score variants (VCF) or genomic regions (BED) using log-likelihood ratios
by calculating the difference in log-likelihood between reference and alternate alleles

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: l20: 20M; l24: 40M; l28: 112M (paper Table 1 and model card) or 128M (README table); l32: 225M. The README warns that on some Transformers versions weight tying breaks and the reported count doubles.
facts.source_locator: Model card: Model Overview; README: Model summary; Paper: Table 1

quotes.text: resulting in models ranging from 20 million to 225 million parameters
On some versions of Transformers, weight tying can break resulting in double the amount of apparent parameters.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: 16 angiosperm genomes spanning about 160 million years, split into 512-bp windows with a 256-bp step; noncoding regions were down-sampled and repeats down-weighted. For hexaploid wheat only subgenome A was used. The Brassicales genomes came from the GPN dataset. The pretraining set is on Hugging Face as kuleshov-group/Angiosperm_16_genomes.

run_guide.summary: Install the repository environment at a pinned commit on an NVIDIA GPU machine, load PlantCaduceus_l32 from Hugging Face and compute strand-averaged embeddings for one 512-bp sequence.
prerequisites: An NVIDIA GPU with CUDA; the README quick example uses device 'cuda:0'. The repository's benchmark gives PlantCaduceus_l32 a peak memory of 1.1 GB at batch size 16 and 512 bp.
conda, to create a Python 3.11 environment. requirements.txt pins torch==2.5.1 (CUDA 12.4 wheels) and transformers==4.49.0.
mamba-ssm 2.2.4 and causal-conv1d 1.5.0.post8, built without build isolation.
Code and weights are Apache-2.0 and the weights are not gated.

steps.shell:

cd PlantCaduceus
git checkout --detach 5f28c156dfa16af03e1c704a79a7b2f6c39013c7
steps.explanation: The clone and cd lines are from the local installation guide, which use the kuleshov-group URL; the README's issue links point to plantcad/plantcad. The checkout line is added to pin the commit this page was written from.

steps.title: Create the environment
steps.shell:
conda create -n PlantCAD python=3.11
conda activate PlantCAD
pip install -r requirements.txt
python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
steps.explanation: Creates the conda environment, installs the pinned packages and checks that PyTorch sees the GPU.
steps.source_locator: docs/local-install.md: Local installation, Verify torch; requirements.txt

steps.title: Install mamba-ssm
steps.explanation: Installs the Mamba kernels that the Caduceus model code imports.

steps.title: Compute embeddings
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForMaskedLM

device = 'cuda:0'
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('kuleshov-group/PlantCaduceus_l32')
model = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained(
    'kuleshov-group/PlantCaduceus_l32', trust_remote_code=True
).to(device)

sequence = ""

input_ids = tokenizer.encode_plus(
    sequence, return_tensors="pt", return_attention_mask=False,
    return_token_type_ids=False
)["input_ids"].to(device)

with torch.inference_mode():
    outputs = model(input_ids=input_ids, output_hidden_states=True)

embeddings = outputs.hidden_states[-1].to(torch.float32).cpu().numpy()

# Average forward and reverse complement embeddings
hidden_size = embeddings.shape[-1] // 2
forward = embeddings[..., 0:hidden_size]
reverse = embeddings[..., hidden_size:][:, ::-1, :]
averaged_embeddings = (forward + reverse) / 2
print(averaged_embeddings.shape)
PY
steps.explanation: The README 'Quick example' wrapped in a shell heredoc. It downloads PlantCaduceus_l32, runs one 512-bp sequence on the GPU and averages the forward and reverse-complement halves of the last hidden state.

outputs: The shape of the strand-averaged embedding array: one row per token of the input sequence, with half the width of the raw hidden state. The README does not print the expected numbers.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.

The repository now also hosts PlantCAD2 (Cell Genomics 2026), a separate model with 8192-bp context; it may deserve its own record and was kept out of this page. Parameter count for l28 conflicts: 112M in the paper and card, 128M in the README. The GENEB leaderboard evaluated PlantCaduceus_l32 (params 225000000), which matches the sources.
